title: Track Rust mod/use statements as import edges
description:
sutra currently does not track Rust `mod` declarations or `use` statements as import edges in the dependency graph. This means constraints scoped to Rust files (`no_cycles`, `max_fan_in`) bind to zero files and are inert.

Discovered during pyswisseph-rs/9 checkpoint review: `wrapper-no-cycles` (scope `src/**`) shows `matched_file_count: {"scope": 0}` despite 7 indexed Rust files with 364 symbols. `sutra_deps(path="src/lib.rs")` returns zero edges.

This blocks Rust-side architectural governance for any sutra-governed Rust project. The pyswisseph-rs constraints (`wrapper-no-cycles`, `wrapper-fan-in`) are correctly authored but architecturally toothless until this lands.

acceptance_criteria.text: mod foo; declarations (external module declarations) produce import edges in the dependency graph
sutra_deps returns non-zero edges for Rust projects with module structure
no_cycles and max_fan_in constraints bind to Rust files when scoped via scope/target globs
Inline modules (mod foo { ... }) do NOT produce spurious import edges
Existing use statement import resolution continues to work unchanged
Unit tests cover mod declaration extraction and resolution

execution_record: Single-file change as planned. Added mod_item detection to walk_imports_recursive in src/parser/rust.rs — 14 lines of production code, 25 lines of tests. No changes needed to resolution pipeline, DB schema, or constraint evaluation. All 1113 tests pass.

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex review: needs-attention (1 finding).

[high] Nested mod declarations inside inline modules resolve to wrong file. `mod outer { mod inner; }` in src/lib.rs emits `self::inner` which resolves to src/inner.rs instead of src/outer/inner.rs. This was acknowledged as a known limitation in the plan but could produce false edges if the wrong file exists.

Recommendation: thread inline module prefix through walk_imports_recursive to synthesize e.g. `self::outer::inner`."
